verdict.rationale: Crawl4AI documents several of its own controls over when content is captured and how much is gathered. It can execute JS and wait for async or sync dynamic content, cap a deep crawl with --max-pages, and use adaptive crawling that stops once enough information is gathered. It also offers a faster prefetch mode for URL discovery and full-page scrolling for completeness. However, the evidence never shows fine-grained control over exactly when content is returned. missing for 10: documented wait-condition or timeout parameters (e.g. selector or network-idle waits), streaming or early-return of partial results, explicit latency-vs-completeness guidance or benchmarks, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trade off latency against completeness by controlling exactly when content is returned
